newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Fairfield County economy perks up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Fairfield County economy perks up in 1996.

text.p: The economy of Fairfield County in southwestern Connecticut perked up this year, a county business group said in a statement released late Tuesday night.
The county's economy reached an overall "healthy" level in 1996, as unemployment and vacancy rates reached lows unseen since the early 1980s, said The Fairfield County Information Exchange.
Retail and housing sales also grew dramatically over 1995, and small- and mid-sized firms continued to move in from greater New York City, the Information Exchange said.
Some 34 firms moved to the county this year, up from 30 in 1995.
Among them were Philip Morris Capital Corp., which moved to Stamford from Rye Brook, N.Y., and Creditanstalt-Bankverein.

In addition, SBC-Warburg, the international banking division of Swiss Bank Corp, is building a new corporate complex in Stamford which will be ready for occupancy in the fall of 1997, the Information Exchange said.
The county's office vacancy rates dropped to 14.7 percent as of the third quarter, against 17.1 percent in 1995.
The area also achieved virtually full employment, with the unemployment rate dropping to 3.8 percent from 3.93 percent last year, the Information Exchange said.
Housing sales through the third quarter increased by 7.92 percent to 12,164. The average median price of a home grew by more than $12,000 to $262,485.
The biggest increases in home sales occurred in the towns of Bethel, Danbury, Easton, Sherman, Stamford, Weston, Westport and Wilton.
"Based on income, employment and housing data, southwestern Connecticut is outperforming all other areas of the state," said Don Klepper-Smith, president of Datacore Partners.
The county's retail sales climbed 4.49 percent to $10.3 billion by June of this year. This made up about 31 percent of Connecticut's total retail sales income.
Some four companies moved out of Fairfield County this year, including Nine West Group, Ultramar Corp, The Pittston Co, and Smith Corona Corp.
